judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures are exact, and the judge's itemisation survives a line-by-line check. Problem 3 asks "What is each pair worth, and how many pairs are there?" - verify.json id 3 is a lone `series` (2k-1, k=1..10 -> 100), so the pair value 20 and pair count 5 are unchecked. Problem 5(a) asks for the signed common difference - id 5 checks only a12 = -13. Problem 6(a) asks for the last row - id 6 checks only the total 348, not 40. Problem 9(a) says "Find the 20th term first" - id 9 checks only the sum 820, not 79. Problem 10 asks (a) how many common differences separate the 4th and 9th terms and (c) the first term - id 10 checks only d=4, so 5 and a1=2 are unchecked. Problem 11(a) asks for the explicit formula for row k - id 11 checks only the capacity 615. And the explanations are real: problem 7(a) "Explain in one sentence where the 4 and the 3 come from" and problem 12(c) "Explain in one sentence why that overestimates" have no manual entry; gate_log.txt reports "13 passed - 0 failed - 0 manual" and final_response.md states "All 12 worksheet problems (13 verify entries) are machine-verified - 0 manual items". I recomputed every keyed value and all are correct (33, 31, 100, 11, -13, 348, 103, 11, 820, 4, 615, 405, 5250), including the two I had to derive myself: a1 = 14 - 3*4 = 2 and the last row 18 + 11*2 = 40.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 3 develops the sum formula from the pairing argument instead of handing it over, and its check is a genuine `series` summation of 2k-1 over k=1..10 rather than an evaluation of the closed form the key prints - so SymPy re-derives the total instead of confirming the author's own algebra. Every total on the sheet (ids 3, 6, 9, 11, 12) is checked this way.

Problem 10 gives two NON-consecutive terms (a4=14, a9=34), which forces the student to count the five steps between them rather than reading d off adjacent values - the one item on the sheet that cannot be answered by pattern-matching.

The six declared traps target the single dominant error in finite sums and derive their numbers: 20*(3+19*4)=1580 for "last term times number of terms", 15*62=930 for the theatre, 12*18=216 for ignoring the growth, 20*405=8100 on the synthesis item. The key's "Common wrong answers" block turns each into a grading sentence.

The directions name the decision the interleaving is built around - "Decide first whether the question asks for one term, for which term, or for a total" - and the facets then rotate so no more than three consecutive problems share one.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md's verification contract has a per-PROBLEM floor, not a per-RESPONSE-SLOT floor: "verification hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check". A multi-part sheet therefore satisfies the gate with one scalar per id, and build.sh prints "0 manual" - which reads as "everything on this sheet was checked" rather than "every id had something checked". This case is the clearest demonstration in my batch: six problems print lettered sub-answers and each is certified by one entry covering the LAST part. The file even shows the correct pattern - id 12 carries two entries (405 and 5250) - so the shape is available and was simply not required.
evidence: problem 3 "(a) What is each pair worth, and how many pairs are there?" -- id 3 is a lone series entry (100)
problem 5 "(a) What is the common difference d? Write it with its sign." -- id 5 checks only a12 = -13
problem 6 "(a) How many seats are in the last row?" -- id 6 checks only the total 348
problem 9 "(a) Find the 20th term first." -- id 9 checks only the sum 820
problem 10 "(a) How many common differences ... (c) Find the first term a1." -- id 10 checks only d = 4
problem 11 "(a) Write the explicit formula for the number of seats in row k." -- id 11 checks only 615
verify.json id 12 carries TWO entries, proving the multi-entry shape is available

root_causes.description: SKILL.md line 257 already says it plainly - "Use `manual` for: graph sketches, sign charts, word problem setups, two-column proofs, constructions, ... and any explanation/reasoning answer" - but line 249 immediately narrows it ("Reserve `manual` for genuinely open reasoning") and tells the author to reframe error analysis "via the ordinary types". Read together, the guidance reads as a licence to type an explanation-bearing problem by its numeric half. Nothing in the gate chain notices, because no gate reads the problem prose looking for a demanded explanation.
evidence: problem 7(a): "Explain in one sentence where the 4 and the 3 come from." -- id 7 is a lone eval (103)
problem 12(c): "Explain in one sentence why that overestimates, and say what the correct averaging idea is." -- id 12's two entries are eval and series, neither manual
final_response.md: "All 12 worksheet problems (13 verify entries) are machine-verified - 0 manual items."

root_causes.description: final_response.md names the three documents only by role ("the student worksheet, a full step-by-step answer key, and a two-page skills summary") and never gives a filename or path, although gate_log.txt printed all three. Eight of the ten cases in my batch print the ws_/ak_/ss_ names; this one and curr-276 do not.
evidence: final_response.md contains no ".pdf", no "ws_", "ak_" or "ss_" token, and no output path
gate_log.txt's PDFs block lists all three generated files
SKILL.md step 6: "report the three output paths clearly"

improvements.title: One verify entry per printed response slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Change the coverage rule in SKILL.md from "every id 1..N has at least one check" to "every printed response slot has a check", and enforce it mechanically: add a slot counter to tests/check_layout.py (which already parses the worksheet .tex for answer-location macros) that counts, per problem, the lettered parts ((a)/(b)/(c)), the blank cells of a fill-in table, and each answer line, then reports when a problem's verify entries number fewer than its slots. Multi-entry ids are already legal and already used in these same files, so the fix adds entries, not machinery.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 2 prints "(a) ... (b) ... (c) ..." with a verify JSON holding a single eval entry for id 2. Assert the gate chain flags problem 2 with the two uncovered parts named. Today the chain exits 0 and the delivery text claims full verification.
improvements.expected_impact: Multi-part problems stop being certified on the strength of their last line. Across this batch the same shape appears in curr-252, curr-256, curr-275, curr-276 and curr-300.
improvements.risk: Medium: counting slots from .tex will over-count where a lettered part is rhetorical rather than a response. Ship as exit 2 (manual visibility) before promoting to exit 1, so a correct build is never blocked by a parse artefact.

improvements.title: Sub-part explanations on a sequences sheet need manual entries
improvements.proposed_change: Apply the manual rule per response slot, not per problem: ids 7 and 12 each gain a `manual` entry alongside their numeric checks (id 7: "the 4 is the common difference / slope and the 3 is the term-zero value a1 - d"; id 12: "multiplying the best week by 20 assumes every week matched week 20; the sum uses the AVERAGE of first and last"). Both descs already exist as prose in answer_key.pdf. Back it with the prose lint in tests/check_layout.py described for this cluster.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 3(b) reads "Explain in one sentence why that overestimates" with a verify JSON holding only eval and series entries for id 3. Assert the build exits 2 with problem 3 listed manual; today it exits 0 and the delivery text claims 0 manual items.
improvements.expected_impact: The two written explanations move inside the declared boundary and the "0 manual items" claim in final_response.md becomes true rather than merely consistent with the gate.
improvements.risk: Medium: a verb lint over problem prose will fire on stems that use "explain" inside a hint rather than as a demand. Ship it as exit 2 (manual-review visibility), which is the honest outcome anyway and cannot block a correct build.

improvements.title: Delivery text names the three documents only by role, never by filename or path
improvements.proposed_change: SKILL.md step 6 says to "report the three output paths clearly". Make that mechanical rather than advisory: have build.sh's final summary emit a copy-ready delivery block containing the three PDF paths it already prints under its PDFs heading, and state in SKILL.md step 6 that the delivery message must reproduce those three paths verbatim.
improvements.regression_test: Harness check over evals/runs/*/tasks/*/final_response.md asserting each contains all three PDF basenames printed in that task's gate_log.txt PDFs block. It fails today for this case and passes once the delivery text quotes them.
improvements.expected_impact: A reader of the delivery message can tell which of the three files is which and where to find them, matching the eight other cases in this batch that do print the ws_/ak_/ss_ names.
improvements.risk: Low. Purely additive to the delivery text; no artefact or gate behaviour changes.

case_summary: Excellent sequences material - the pairing argument is developed rather than asserted, every total is checked by a real `series` summation instead of the closed form, problem 10 forces step-counting from two non-consecutive terms, and six derived traps target the "last term times n" error. All thirteen keyed values are correct under independent recomputation. The rejection is right and the judge's itemisation is exact: six problems print lettered sub-answers (pair value and count, signed d, last row, twentieth term, step count and a1, the row-k formula) whose only check covers the final part, and problems 7 and 12 demand written explanations on a sheet the gate log and the delivery text both report as 0 manual. One finding the judge did not raise: final_response.md never names a filename or path for any of the three PDFs.
